sample_rule: prose paragraphs (no headings/code/tables/math lines) counted from the body; paragraph 3 then every third (3, 6, 9, ... 135) gave 45 paragraphs; 15 claims taken from them

score_notes.A: Front matter fine (two-level categories, use_math with $$). Deductions: facts stated twice across sections (user_config no restart, host/port fixed, rolling_update_percentage (0.0, 1.0] at L710 and again L796); Sources list omits works the body cites (Suhas Bhairav's Triton blog L986/L995, the discuss.ray.io thread L800, the Serve LLM observability page L982) and lists an unrelated page ('take_batch' Ray Data, L1026).
score_notes.B: Mostly natural. TL;DR (L13-15) restates section 1 (L19, L30, L34, L36) nearly sentence for sentence; '결국 모델마다 자원과 레플리카 수를 따로 정해야 하는데' (L21) and '장애 복구는 결국 ...로 정리됩니다' (L93) are formulaic; '단일 진실 공급원' (L577, L824) is a calque (rewrite: '설정의 기준 파일'); the last heading (L984) '독립 확장이 필요한 Python 파이프라인에 맞고 모델별 최적화 서버로는 부족한 선택지' is overlong.
score_notes.C: Running example threads through cleanly. '(앞서 다룬 스케일링 기본 요소)' (L997) points back to a term never introduced; the Ray 2017-paper section (L155-185) is a detour whose scheduler worked example concerns placement, not Serve request routing (the post says so itself at L183).
score_notes.D: Good worked examples where it is hard: power-of-two-choices table (L124-132), 2x4 concurrency arithmetic (L841), fractional GPU arithmetic (L871). Some padding: chain replication definition (L167), cost formula for global scheduler.
score_notes.E: Tables and code placed where discussed. Deduction: the 'serve build가 막 출력한 파일' YAML (L661-682) is not real tool output; Ray 2.60.0 serve build on the post's own text_ml.py emits name app1, a logging_config block, grpc enable_reflection, and deployments without num_replicas. ASCII figures are marked as illustrations.
score_notes.F: One wrong claim in the sample (backpressure 500) plus out-of-sample wrong statements: backpressure_config.status_code said not to apply behind a handle (L839, disproven at runtime), invented serve build output (L661-682), the official ray-project architecture.md labelled '서드파티 문서' (L97, L794), a cited blog with no link (Bhairav). The working-dir sentence (L749) omits the CLI's 'Ignored when deploying from a config file', which is the reader's path.
score_notes.T1: Running example runs as pasted on Ray 2.60.0 (see runnable_code). Gaps: multi-app YAML imports model:translator_app but no model.py is ever named (L811); the RayService serveConfigV2 (L767-790) has no working_dir, so pods cannot import text_ml although the text says to copy it '그대로' (L763); the FastAPI Translator file is unnamed.
score_notes.T2: Covers concepts, composition, HTTP/FastAPI, config, KubeRay, scaling, observability in a sensible order; Ray-paper scheduler section is somewhat padded relative to Serve.
score_notes.T3: Strong on architecture, request path, fault-tolerance owners, observability. Weak spot: the scaling section never shows autoscaling_config (min/max_replicas, target_ongoing_requests, delays) although autoscaling is a tag and the autoscaler's placement is discussed (L134-140); design advice mostly reads as recommendation.

examples.claim: Four actor kinds; by default one HTTP proxy actor on the head node, optionally one per node
examples.source: docs.ray.io serve/architecture: 'HTTP Proxy: By default there is one HTTP proxy actor on the head node ... run a proxy on each node ... via the proxy_location field' (page says 'three kinds' but lists Controller, HTTP proxy, gRPC proxy, Replicas). Note: post calls this official doc '서드파티 문서'.

examples.claim: Danshyn: CoreWorker processes inference requests as actor tasks; each CoreWorker has a TaskCounter tracking pending/running/finished
examples.source: themutex.substack.com/p/ray-serve-autoscaling: 'Every instance of CoreWorker has a TaskCounter that tracks the numbers of pending, running and finished tasks. HTTP requests for model inference end up being processed by CoreWorker as actor tasks.'

examples.claim: serve run blocks and streams logs; Ctrl-C shuts down Serve on the cluster; import path may point to an Application or a function taking key=val args
examples.source: serve run --help (Ray 2.60.0): 'Passed import paths must point to an Application object or a function that returns one ... arguments can be passed to it in key=val format ... If you Ctrl-C the command, it will shut down Serve on the cluster.'

examples.claim: TF and sklearn tutorial clients use requests.get with json= to localhost:8000; PyTorch posts data=ray_logo_bytes
DeploymentResponseGenerator usable sync/async; sync use inside a deployment blocks the replica; cannot be passed to other handle calls
examples.source: serve/model_composition: 'avoid using a DeploymentResponseGenerator as a sync generator within a deployment ... Note that you can't pass DeploymentResponseGenerators to other handle calls.'

examples.claim: asyncio.shield() protects async calls but cannot be used on a DeploymentHandle call
examples.source: serve/http-guide: 'Note that asyncio.shield cannot be used on a DeploymentHandle call to prevent the downstream handler from being cancelled.'

examples.claim: serve build output also contains a grpc_options block (port 9000) and an empty runtime_env
examples.source: serve/production-guide/config: generated file shows 'grpc_options: port: 9000' and 'runtime_env: {}'; 'the runtime_env field will always be empty when using serve build'. (The YAML block that follows in the post is not the real output; see issues.)

examples.claim: serve deploy --working-dir must be a remote .zip URI (e.g. S3)
examples.source: serve deploy --help: 'This must be a remote URI to a .zip file (e.g., S3 bucket)' - the post omits the same help text's 'Ignored when deploying from a config file.'

examples.claim: discuss.ray.io answer linking Ray 2.51.2 docs: one HTTP server (one port) per cluster; use multi-app route prefixes /service1, /service2, single YAML under RayService; Ingress/NGINX for ports
examples.source: discuss.ray.io/t/23403 answer (by the RunLLM bot) with links to github ray releases/2.51.2 production-guide/kubernetes.md. Thread is not in the post's Sources list.

examples.claim: max_queued_requests is per caller (proxy or handle), default -1 (no limit); handles get BackPressureError, HTTP gets 503 by default
examples.source: ray.serve.schema: 'queued at each caller (proxy or DeploymentHandle) ... raise a BackPressureError (for handles) or return an HTTP 503 status code by default ... Defaults to -1 (no limit).'

examples.claim: If Summarizer does not catch the BackPressureError from the Translator handle, the client gets 500, not 503
examples.source: Ray 2.60.0 local test: ingress -> handle -> inner deployment (max_ongoing_requests=1, max_queued_requests=1), 6 concurrent HTTP requests, no try/except: codes [200, 503, 503, 503, 503, 503]; with backpressure_config status_code 429 on the inner deployment: [200, 429 x5], body 'Request dropped due to backpressure'. So L839's 'not applicable behind a handle' is also wrong.

examples.claim: Python Data Bench: num_gpus 0.25 lets four lightweight models share one A10G; for embedding models cuts cost per prediction 3-4x
examples.source: pythondatabench.com: 'four lightweight models share a single A10G. For embedding models that don't saturate a full GPU, this cuts cost per prediction by 3-4x.'
